title: Beautiful, and Not
label: ch:ml-beauty
canDo: I can say that something is beautiful, name beauty itself, and deny it.

payoff.summary: From cold: both ends of one quality, and which letter arrives when aaNu follows a word.
payoff.note: Three atoms. THE FIRST DRAFT UNIFIED TWO DIFFERENT PROCESSES -- 'a letter arrives' is false for the anusvara, which already IS the m and only changes how it is written, and true only for bhangi/kutti where a ya is genuinely added between two vowels. It also taught that alla does not weld, read out of ML-C77's single chillu-final example, the one host that cannot show the rule; alla welds exactly as aaNu does and the headword is now ithu sundaramalla. The recall's 'nothing else' was falsified by its own title romanization sundaravum. ithu bhangiyaaNu means THIS IS BEAUTIFUL, not 'this is beauty'. The romanization is bhamgi, since the track reserves the nga letter for nga and writes a medial anusvara with the dotted m, as in kumbham. ROUND TWO OF REVIEW CAUGHT A FALSEHOOD IN THE FIX ITSELF: the correction explained that chapter 77's njaan adhyaapakan alla looks separate BECAUSE the host ends in a chillu, 'a consonant with no vowel to pass on'. That is false and two lessons the learner has already seen refute it -- ML-C36-makan has ithu ente makanaaNu and ML-C87 teaches adhyaapakane, the same word with the chillu going back to na. The chillu is in fact the EXACT ANALOGUE of the anusvara, a consonant written without a vowel that reverts to its full letter when one arrives, so the true version reinforces two earlier chapters instead of contradicting them. Also reverted an over-correction: the headword gloss was changed to 'beautiful' when bhangi is a noun, 'beauty' -- only the SENTENCE means 'this is beautiful'. And the glide is now credited to ML-C70-um, which already taught it at ariyum, rather than presented as new.
